newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late rubber stable in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late rubber stable in quiet trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were stable in late trading on Wednesday, with hardly any sign of buyers as the market remained under a cloud following news of high Thai stocks, traders said.
"There were no transactions today," one trader said. "Buyers seem to have vanished following news of Thailand's stock levels as announced in Bali."

The traders said a Thai industry official who attended a gathering of regional rubber produers on the tourist island of Bali over the weekend had told the meeting that Thailand had stock levels of about 140,000 tonnes.
They said the announcement had given the Indonesian market a bearish tone that is expected to last through the week.
"I don't expect any turnaround this week," one trader said. "Prices are likely to weaken because there seems to be no buying interest out there following the Thai news."

Traders said producing countries such as Indonesia and Malaysia are expected to face increasing competition from Thailand, the world's top producer, as Bangkok produces more technically specified rubber than smoked sheets.
"Thai rubber prices have to be attractive in order for them to be able to sell to Europe and the United States, which are traditional markets of Indonesia and Malaysia," one said.
"I think the process of switching from sheet rubber to technically specified rubber in Thailand is much faster than can be taken up by the U.S. and European markets," he added.
He said Thailand's buyers in China and Japan were not ready to absorp all of Bangkok's technically specified rubber, and so Thai players had to look to the United States and Europe.
Traders said September/October SIR20 was offered at 43.75-44.00 cents/lb fob Medan and 43.50-43.75 cents fob Palembang and Padang.
